title: Ultrafast Physical Random Bit Generation Based on an Integrated Mutual Injection DFB Laser
content: Ultrafast physical random bit generators (PRBGs) are essential components for modern applications in secure communication, quantum cryptography, and artificial intelligence. While optical chaos-based PRBGs offer high-speed capabilities, conventional systems often rely on discrete components that suffer from system complexity and environmental instability. This paper proposes and experimentally demonstrates a robust, integrated solution using a two-section mutual injection DFB laser. The device was fabricated using the reconstruction equivalent chirp (REC) technique, which provides precise control over grating phase variation while utilizing low-cost, high-volume fabrication methods.The laser sections, each measuring 450 m in length, were designed with a free-running wavelength difference of 0.3 nm to ensure a flat optical spectrum and enhanced chaotic dynamics. By optimizing the bias currents, we achieved a chaos RF bandwidth of 20.1 GHz. Notably, the resulting chaotic signal lacks time-delayed signatures, which simplifies the randomness extraction process. To generate random bits, the chaotic waveform was sampled by an 8-bit analog-to-digital converter at 100 Gb/s. Following post-processing through delay-subtracting and the extraction of the four least significant bits (4-LSBs), we realized a total physical random bit rate of 400 Gb/s. The randomness of the generated sequence was successfully verified using the NIST SP 800-22 statistical test suite. This approach offers a compact, energy-efficient, and high-performance integrated chaotic source suitable for secure communication and high-performance computation.
